listing.aiSummary: Provides an optimal autofit algorithm for balancing entire fleets based on ship roles, available weapons, and hullmods.

description:
Auto Outfitting
"Optimal" autofit for Starsector 0.98a+0.98.5a.

Source code
Required mods: None. LunaLib is optional and adds a settings menu (F3).
Updating: Delete the old Auto Outfitting folder in mods/, then extract the new one. Or use TriOS.
Safe to add mid-game

Safe to remove mid-game

No required mods

Disclaimer
Just to preface this whole thing, it's all built on the numbers for every weapon, hull and ship I could dig up, from vanilla and from all the mods I had installed.

It's not always optimal, and it won't always do as well as a loadout you build by hand. It's "optimal" in that it tries to balance your whole fleet in one shot with little to no effort from you.

That is the goal of this entire mod. I apologize, I wish it could be perfection but it sure ain't, lmao. Enjoy anyway if you see fit.

Buttons
Optimize fleet and Order fleet weapons both work out a plan from every ship in your fleet and the weapons and hullmods you've found or unlocked. Optimize fleet puts the fits on your ships using what you already have. Order fleet weapons orders whatever the plan is still missing through custom production, the vanilla one or the AoTD one.
Optimal (in the refit screen's Autofit list): Fits the selected ship from the weapons, fighters and hullmods available to it, using the mod's own scoring. A hand-built fit can be better.
Optimize fleet: Hitting it brings up a settings panel first, so you can set up how you want the fleet optimized before it starts running anything. All the tick boxes are on there: using storage at the market you're docked at, stripping stored ships, buying from the shops, building in s-mods, changing s-mods with credits, placing officers, and placing augments. It remembers what you picked per save. Once you hit Plan fleet it plans every combat ship in the fleet together from one shared stock, biggest ships first, and lists each ship's changes and CR cost. Settings takes you back to the panel if you want to change something. Apply to all ships puts the fits on. With Place officers ticked, officers move to the ship where they add the most. The player and AI cores stay where they are.
Order fleet weapons: Lists the weapons and fighters the fleet plan is missing, with prices, budget and where it gets delivered. Queue all orders them through custom production. Pressing it again later orders only what is still missing.
Fleet analysis: Shows the fleet's damage mix, fighter roles and weak spots. Changes nothing.
Lock this ship: A button on the refit screen that keeps a ship out of Optimize fleet and Order fleet weapons. Its weapons don't get used for other ships either.

How ships are fitted

Stock: Optimal uses the sources ticked in the Autofit panel (cargo, storage, market, black market). Optimize fleet uses what's already mounted on the ships, fleet cargo, and the storage of the market you are docked at (when Use storage here is ticked), plus the shops if you tick them. Order fleet weapons counts cargo and storage at every market, so it does not order what you already have.
Scoring: Weapons and hullmods are picked on combat numbers and on how the game's AI flies the ship. The officer's skills, d-mods and CR count. Scores are estimates from stats and tables. No combat is simulated.
Roles: Every ship gets fitted for the job it's actually good at, going off its designation and its numbers: how fast it is compared to other ships its size, its ship system, and whether it's a phase ship, carrier, missile boat, etc. Fast frigates get fitted to grab points, keep enemies busy, run down weak ships and not die, and they get some credit for being able to outrun what they're fighting (more with a Phase Skimmer or Phase Teleporter). Slow, tough ships like the Enforcer and Dominator get fitted as brawlers. AI support carriers (Heron, Condor, Astral) only get point defense and missiles so they hang back with their fighters, and the Mora, Drover, Gemini and Colossus Mk.III get fitted as battle carriers since the AI flies them like line ships anyway.
Flagship: The ship you're flying gets its own fit, one that can do everything on its own. It fights every ship size, carries its own point defense, and has both kinetic and armor-cracking damage, while still keeping its specialty (a carrier flagship is still a carrier, it just gets real guns too). Optimize fleet plans it first so it gets first pick of the weapons, and special ships (Ziggurat, Remnant, Omega, anything no blueprint builds) go before the other ships their size. If you'd rather it get a normal fit, turn off Balanced flagship in the settings.
Buying: Optimize fleet can buy weapons and LPCs from the shops at the market you're docked at. There are two ticks for it, one for the legal shops and one for the black markets (modded ones count too, like Underworld's Cabal Exchange). It pays the same prices the refit screen shows you, tariffs and all. You also set how much of your credits it's allowed to spend: 10%, 25%, 50%, 75% or all of it, 25% by default. Bigger ships get to buy first, and if a ship would go over the limit it just uses what you already own.
Civilian ships: Freighters, tankers and salvage ships get campaign hullmods and no weapons. OP left over goes into vents and capacitors.
S-mods: Only built in when Build in s-mods is ticked: in the Autofit panel for Optimal, and on the settings panel for Optimize fleet. It always leaves you at least 5 story points (you can change that).
S-mods on small ships: S-mods lean pretty heavily towards bigger ships now. A fleet of frigates with three s-mods each, when those story points could have gone into capitals, is kind of ridiculous, so frigates get 1 s-mod at most and destroyers 2 (s-mods they already have count). A small ship also needs a much bigger gain before it gets one at all (the gain it needs is up to 4 times higher for a 5 DP frigate, and half as much for a 40 DP capital). All of that is in the LunaLib settings if you want it different.
Changing s-mods: There's a tick on the Optimize fleet panel for the game's own Change s-mods with credits. It only works at your own colony with heavy industry, and it's expensive: 75,000 to 250,000 credits per s-mod removed or added depending on hull size, no story points. So it's off by default, and when it's on it gets used pretty sparingly. It only touches ships whose s-mod slots are all full, the ship has to come out at least 10% stronger (more for small ships), and the cost has to fit in your credit limit. It also won't pull an s-mod off and then build it back in with a story point in the same run.

Getting started

Open the refit screen and pick a ship.
Press Autofit, then click Optimal.
Press Confirm to keep it.

Screenshots
Refit screen: the Order fleet weapons and Optimize fleet buttons.

Optimize fleet: the plan before Apply to all ships.

Order fleet weapons: planning progress, then the order before Queue all.

Compatibility

Modded ships: Ships, weapons, fighters, hullmods and ship systems from any mod are rated from their loaded stats. Mods under Supported mods also get rules for their scripted effects.
Fleet Toolkit: Nothing to change with its default settings. If its Autofit Menu is on, its "Replace Vanilla Button" setting decides which menu the Autofit button opens. Optimal is in the game's menu, so turn that setting off. Optimize fleet and Order fleet weapons are separate buttons.
Ship Mastery System: Turn off its "S-mod autofit option" in LunaLib, or its autofit replaces Optimal.
Bugs: Post here or open a GitHub issue with starsector-core/starsector.log and your modlist.

Supported mods
All optional. Each integration turns on when its mod is enabled.
Large integrations
LunaLib Settings menu (F3).
MagicLib Weapon interference penalties from every mod that sets them.
Ashes of the Domain (Vaults of Knowledge) Order fleet weapons uses AoTD production. Entropy Lance is not fitted.
Random Assortment of Things Order fleet weapons orders at a Frontiers settlement. Alterations stay on ships. Chronos range cap and weapon effects counted.
Emergent Threats (and IX Revival) AI Subsystem Integration is never built in. Drone-only bays, Trinity Worlds drones and range, adaptive subsystems, seeker lenses, repair nanites and weapon effects counted.
United Aurora Federation Secondary Focus bonus, hullmods and weapon effects counted.
Seeker - Unidentified Contact Plague hulls fly plague LPCs only. Plague weapons and LPCs cost CR on other hulls.
Weapon effects
Tahlan Shipworks Weapon effects. Hull rules for Legio Infernalis, Stahlherz and Glanzwurf. Manannan is not fitted.
Diable Avionics Weapon effects. Weapon selectors in built-in slots stay.
Knights of Ludd Weapon effects. Lidar and Knight Refit rules.
Amazigh's Ship Foundry, Valkyrian, Roider Union Weapon effects and hull rules.
Interstellar Imperium, Stardust Ventures, Ship/Weapon Pack, Tri-Tac Expansion, Junk Yard Dogs, Hillock Prototype and Station Tech, Jackundor's Advanced Arms Weapon script effects counted (explosions, arcs, extra hits).
Secrets of the Frontier, THREAT TECH Weapon effects. Fragment weapons scored by the ship's fragment swarm.
Hullmods
Arma Armatura Hullmods with no stat effect are not used as filler.
Industrial.Evolution Weapon effects. Forge World Experiment stats read per ship.
Yunru's Arsenal, Yunru's Hullmods, YunruCore Install hullmods and Let's Bayblade! are not added. Weapon effects counted.
Ship Mastery System Its s-mod slots count. Turn off its S-mod autofit option in LunaLib.
AI Tweaks, Starship Legends Their hullmods stay through refits. Starship Legends traits count.
Omega Core Everywhere, There Be Juggernaughts, What We Left Behind, Attuned Drive Field Hullmod rules.
Treasure Hunt Treasure Hunt Package valued on civilian ships.
Advanced Modifications Combat effects counted. Hullmods that use up cores or transplutonics go only on ships that already paid.
Extra System Reloaded - Oddisz Edition Its hullmod stays through refits. Optimize fleet puts each augment on the ship where it adds the most, at a friendly market with a spaceport. Augment effects counted in fits.
Other mods
Any other mod Weapons, fighters, hullmods and ship systems rated from their loaded stats.

Mod support requests go here or in GitHub issues.

Permissions: Free to use, change and reupload, in modpacks too. No credit needed. Do not sell it.

AI use disclaimer
Some or all code in this mod was created using AI tools:
Code, docs and offline build checks: Claude Opus 5.5 (through Claude Code).
Design and in-game testing: Mjolniar.
Training data: None added. Art: None.

aiDescription: Automatically fits ships using a scoring system that considers combat stats, AI behavior, and ship designations. It can optimize the whole fleet at once, order missing equipment through production or shops, and manage s-mods and officers.
